in_sanskrit.name: शकुन
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Shakun is a Sanskrit word meaning 'fortunate' or 'auspicious'. It is derived from the Sanskrit verb 'shak', which means 'to have power' or 'to be able'. Shagun signifies the power or ability to bestow blessings or bring good fortune.

in_hindi.name: शागुन
in_hindi.long_meaning: Shagun is a Hindi word that means 'fortunate' or 'auspicious'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'shakun', which means 'fortunate' or 'auspicious'. In Hindi culture, Shagun is often given as a blessing or gift to signify good luck and prosperity.

in_tamil.name: ஷாகுன
in_tamil.long_meaning: Shagun in Tamil means 'the fortune that comes through others'. It is derived from the Tamil word 'shakam', which means 'power' or 'ability'. In Tamil culture, Shagun represents the good fortune or blessings that come through the help and support of others.

in_telugu.name: శాగున
in_telugu.long_meaning: Shagun in Telugu means 'one who is ever auspicious'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'shakun', which means 'fortunate' or 'auspicious'. In Telugu culture, Shagun represents the eternal auspiciousness or blessings that one can bestow upon others.
